parts.text:

A random sample of 36 students is taken from the university.
The random variable $X$ represents the number of these students who are members of the dance club.
(b) Using a suitable model for $X$, find
(i) $\mathrm{P}(X=4)$
(ii) $\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 7)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: [Sight or correct use of] $X \sim \mathrm{B}(36, 0.08)$
(i) A1: $\mathrm{P}(X=4) = 0.167387\ldots$ awrt $0.167$
(ii) A1: $[\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 7) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 6) =] 0.022233\ldots$ awrt $0.0222$ (3)

- M1 for sight of B(36, 0.08) Allow in words: binomial with $n = 36$ and $p = 0.08$ may be implied by one correct answer to 2sf or sight of $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 6) = 0.97776...$ i.e. awrt 0.98. Allow for $36C4 \times 0.08^4 \times 0.92^{32}$ as this is "correct use"

(d) Using your knowledge of the large data set, place each of these Cardinal Wind Directions in the correct location in the table.

(2)

questions.stem:
A large college produces three magazines.
One magazine is about green issues, one is about equality and one is about sports.
A student at the college is selected at random and the events $G$, $E$ and $S$ are defined as follows
$G$ is the event that the student reads the magazine about green issues
$E$ is the event that the student reads the magazine about equality
$S$ is the event that the student reads the magazine about sports
The Venn diagram, where $p$, $q$, $r$ and $t$ are probabilities, gives the probability for each subset.
[Venn diagram: $G$ contains $0.08$ (only), overlap $G \cap E$ (only) $0.05$, $E$ contains $0.09$ (only); overlap $G \cap S$ (only) $q$; centre $G \cap E \cap S$ is $p$; overlap $E \cap S$ (only) $r$; $S$ contains $0.36$ (only); outside all three is $t$.]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the proportion of students in the college who read exactly one of these magazines.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: $0.08 + 0.09 + 0.36 = 0.53$ (1)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for 0.53 (or exact equivalent) [ Allow 53%]

parts.label: b
parts.text:
No students read all three magazines and $\mathrm{P}(G) = 0.25$
(b) Find
(i) the value of $p$
(ii) the value of $q$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(i) B1: $[\mathrm{P}(G \cap E \cap S) = 0 \Rightarrow]$ $p = 0$
(b)(ii) M1: $[\mathrm{P}(G) = 0.25 \Rightarrow]$ $0.08 + 0.05 + q + \text{"}p\text{"} = 0.25$
A1: $q = 0.12$ (3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (i) B1 for $p = 0$ (may be placed in Venn diagram). (ii) M1 for a linear equation for $q$ (ft letter "$p$" or their value if $0 \leqslant p \leqslant 0.12$) $\Rightarrow$ by $p + q = 0.12$. A1 for $q = 0.12$ (may be placed in Venn diagram)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given that $\mathrm{P}(S \mid E) = \frac{5}{12}$
(c) find
(i) the value of $r$
(ii) the value of $t$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) M1: $\left[\mathrm{P}(S \mid E) = \frac{5}{12} \Rightarrow\right]$ $\frac{r + \text{"}p\text{"}}{r + \text{"}p\text{"} + 0.09 + 0.05} = \frac{5}{12}$
A1ft: $[12r = 5r + 5 \times 0.14 \Rightarrow]$ $r = 0.10$
(c)(ii) A1: $r = 0.10$
B1ft: $[0.08 + 0.05 + \text{"}0.12\text{"} + \text{"}0\text{"} + 0.09 + \text{"}0.10\text{"} + 0.36 + t = 1 \Rightarrow]$ $t = 0.20$ (4)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (i) M1 for a ratio of probabilities ($r$ on num and den) (on LHS) with num < den and num or den correct ft. Allow ft of letter "$p$" or their $p$ where $0 \leqslant p < 0.86$ but "+ 0" is not required. 1st A1ft for a correct ratio of probabilities (on LHS) allowing ft of their $p$ where $0 \leqslant p < 0.86$. 2nd A1 for $r = 0.1(0)$ or exact equivalent (may be in Venn diagram) Ans only 3/3. (ii) B1ft for $t = 0.2(0)$ (o.e.) or correct ft i.e. $0.42 - (p + q + r)$ where $p$, $q$, $r$ and $t$ are all probs

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Determine whether or not the events $(S \cap E')$ and $G$ are independent.
Show your working clearly.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1ft: $\mathrm{P}(S \cap E') = 0.36 + \text{"}q\text{"}$ $[=0.48]$
M1: $\mathrm{P}\left([(S \cap E')] \cap G\right) = \text{"}q\text{"}$ $[=0.12]$ and $\mathrm{P}(G) = 0.25$ and $\mathrm{P}(S \cap E') \times \mathrm{P}(G) = \text{"}0.48\text{"} \times \frac{1}{4}$ or $0.12$
A1: $\mathrm{P}(S \cap E') \times \mathrm{P}(G) = 0.12 = \mathrm{P}\left([(S \cap E')] \cap G\right)$ so are independent (3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft for $\mathrm{P}(S \cap E') = 0.48$ (with label) (ft letter "$q$" or their value if $0 \leqslant q \leqslant 0.12$). M1 for attempting all required probs (labelled) and using them in a correct test (allow ft of $q$). A1 for all probs correct and a correct deduction (no ft deduction here)
- SC No "P" If correct argument seen apart from P for probability for all 3 marks, award (B0M1A1). If unsure about an attempt using conditional probabilities, please send to review.

questions.stem:
The heights of females from a country are normally distributed with
• a mean of $166.5\,\mathrm{cm}$
• a standard deviation of $6.1\,\mathrm{cm}$
Given that 1% of females from this country are shorter than $k\,\mathrm{cm}$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the value of $k$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: [Let $F \sim \mathrm{N}(166.5, 6.1^2)$] $\mathrm{P}(F<k) = 0.01 \Rightarrow \frac{k-166.5}{6.1} = -2.3263$
A1: $k = 152.309\ldots$ $152$ or awrt $152.3$ (2)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for standardising (allow $\pm$) with $k$, 166.5 and 6.1 and set equal to a $z$ value $2.3 < |z| < 2.4$. A1 for 152 or awrt 152.3 Ans only 2/2 [Condone poor use of notation e.g. $\mathrm{P}(\frac{k-166.5}{6.1}) = -2.3263$]. Allow percentages instead of probabilities throughout.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the proportion of females from this country with heights between $150\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $175\,\mathrm{cm}$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: $[\mathrm{P}(150 < F < 175) =]$ $0.914840\ldots$ awrt $0.915$ (1)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for awrt 0.915

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A female, from this country, is chosen at random from those with heights between $150\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $175\,\mathrm{cm}$
(c) Find the probability that her height is more than $160\,\mathrm{cm}$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\mathrm{P}(F>160 \mid 150<F<175)$
M1: $= \frac{\mathrm{P}(160<F<175)}{\mathrm{P}(150<F<175)}$ or $\frac{\mathrm{P}(160<F<175)}{\text{"}(b)\text{"}}$
A1ft: $= \frac{0.7749487\ldots}{\text{"}0.91484\ldots\text{"}}$
A1: $= 0.84708\ldots$ awrt $0.847$ (4)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for interpreting demand as an appropriate conditional probability ($\Rightarrow$ by 2nd M1). 2nd M1 for correct ratio of expressions (can ft their (b) on denominator) ($\Rightarrow$ by 1st A1ft). 1st A1ft for a correct ratio of probs (can ft their "0.9148…" to 3sf from (b) if > 0.775). 2nd A1 for awrt 0.847

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The heights of females from a different country are normally distributed with a standard deviation of $7.4\,\mathrm{cm}$
Mia believes that the mean height of females from this country is less than $166.5\,\mathrm{cm}$
Mia takes a random sample of 50 females from this country and finds the mean of her sample is $164.6\,\mathrm{cm}$
(d) Carry out a suitable test to assess Mia's belief.
You should
• state your hypotheses clearly
• use a 5% level of significance
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1: $\mathrm{H_0}: \mu = 166.5$ $\mathrm{H_1}: \mu < 166.5$
M1: [Let $X$ = height of female from 2nd country] $\bar{X} \sim \mathrm{N}\left(166.5, \left(\frac{7.4}{\sqrt{50}}\right)^2\right)$
A1: $\mathrm{P}(\bar{X} < 164.6) = 0.03472\ldots$
dA1: $[0.0347\ldots < 0.05 \text{ so significant or reject } \mathrm{H_0}]$ There is evidence to support Mia's belief (4)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for both correct hypotheses in terms of $\mu$. 1st M1 for selecting the correct model (needn't use $\bar{X}$ $\Rightarrow$ by standardisation or 1st A1). 1st A1 for correct use of the correct model i.e. awrt 0.035 (allow 0.04 if $\mathrm{P}("\bar{X}" < 164.6)$ seen). Condone $\mathrm{P}("\bar{X}" > 164.6) = 0.9652$ or awrt 0.97 only if comparison with 0.95 is made
- ALT Use of $z$ value: Need to see $Z = -1.8(15…)$ and cv of $\pm 1.6449$ (allow 1.64 or better) for 1st A1
- ALT Use of CR or CV for $\bar{X}$: Need to see "$\bar{X}$" < 164.7786… or CV = … (awrt 164.8) for 1st A1. Condone truncation i.e 164.7 or better
- 2nd dA1 (dep on M1A1 only) for a correct inference in context. Must mention Mia's belief or mean height of females/women. Do NOT award if contradictory statements about hypotheses made e.g. "not sig"
- SC M0 for $\bar{X} \sim \mathrm{N}(164.6, …)$ If they achieve $p$ = awrt 0.035 (o.e. with $z$-value or CV of 166.3) and a correct conclusion in context is given score M0A0A1 [and SC for awrt 0.97 > 0.95 case]

questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & a & b & c\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X=x) & \log_{36}a & \log_{36}b & \log_{36}c\\ \hline\end{array}$
where
• $a$, $b$ and $c$ are distinct integers $(a<b<c)$
• all the probabilities are greater than zero

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) the value of $a$
(ii) the value of $b$
(iii) the value of $c$
Show your working clearly.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: [Sum of probs $=1$ implies] $\log_{36}a + \log_{36}b + \log_{36}c = 1$
A1: $\Rightarrow \log_{36}(abc) = 1$ so $abc = 36$
B1: All probabilities greater than 0 implies each of $a$, $b$ and $c > 1$
dM1: $36 = 2^2 \times 3^2$ (or 3 numbers that multiply to give 36 e.g. 2, 2, 9 etc)
A1: Since $a$, $b$ and $c$ are distinct must be $2, 3, 6$ $(a=2, b=3, c=6)$ (5)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for a start to the problem using sum of probabilities leading to eq'n in $a$, $b$ and $c$. 1st A1 for reducing to the equation $abc = 36$ [Must follow from their equation.] NB Can go straight from $abc = 36$ to the answer for full marks for part (a). B1 for deducing that each value > 1 (may be implied by 3 integers all > 1 in the next line). 2nd dM1 (dep on M1A1) for writing 36 as a product of prime factors or 3 values with product = 36 and none = 1. 2nd A1 for 2, 3 and 6 as a list or $a = 2$, $b = 3$ and $c = 6$
- SC Ans only M0M0 If no method marks scored but a correct answer given score: M0A0B1M0A1 (2/5) This gets the SC score of 2/5 [Question says show your working clearly]

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The independent random variables $X_1$ and $X_2$ each have the same distribution as $X$
(b) Find $\mathrm{P}(X_1 = X_2)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $(\log_{36}a)^2 + (\log_{36}b)^2 + (\log_{36}c)^2$
A1: $[= 0.0374137\ldots + 0.09398737\ldots + 0.25]$ $= 0.38140\ldots$ awrt $0.381$ (2)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a correct expression in terms of $a$, $b$ and $c$ or values; ft their integers $a$, $b$ and $c$. Condone invisible brackets if the answer implies they are used. A1 for awrt 0.381
